title: Coq au Vin
subtitle: French chicken braised in red wine with mushrooms and lardons
excerpt: The French country classic: chicken pieces braised in a whole bottle of red wine with lardons, pearl onions, and mushrooms until the wine reduces to a deep, glossy sauce. Rich, warming, and built for a cold evening.

recipe.sourceNotes: Coq au vin (chicken in wine) is one of the most celebrated dishes of French bourgeois cooking, popularised in the English-speaking world by Julia Child's 1961 Mastering the Art of French Cooking. The dish has old peasant roots: a tough old rooster (coq) braised in wine for many hours to tenderise it. Modern versions use younger chicken pieces, which need far less time. The wine is the main ingredient and should be of drinking quality; it is worth using a proper Burgundy or another full-bodied Pinot Noir for an authentic result. The lardons (salt-cured pork belly in batons) are an essential element; pancetta is the best substitute. Pearl onions (small silverskin onions) are browned separately with butter and sugar for the classic garnish; standard onion cannot substitute for this element without changing the character of the dish.

content.text: Use a full bottle of red wine: this is not a dish for the bottle-end. Brown the chicken well in batches; crowding the pan will steam rather than sear it. The sauce needs to reduce until it coats the back of a spoon; thin sauce is the most common fault. If it is too thin at the end of cooking, remove the chicken and simmer the sauce hard for 5 minutes.

items.preparation: a full bottle of good Burgundy or Pinot Noir
small shallots, peeled and left whole

content.text: Season the chicken well. Heat the oil in a large casserole over high heat. Brown the chicken in batches, skin-side down first, for 4 minutes per side until deep golden. Remove. In the same pan, fry the pancetta lardons until golden and the fat has rendered. Remove. Fry the shallots in the butter until browned all over. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute. Add the tomato purée and cook for 1 minute.

Pour in the wine and stock. Add the thyme and bay leaves. Return the chicken and lardons to the pot. The liquid should just cover the chicken; add more stock or water if needed. Bring to a very gentle simmer, cover, and cook for 45 minutes.

Add the mushrooms and cook uncovered for a further 20 to 25 minutes until the sauce has reduced and thickened enough to coat the back of a spoon and the chicken is completely tender. Remove the bay leaves. Taste and adjust the seasoning. Serve scattered with parsley, with mashed potato or crusty bread.
